articles.title: The Sun's Magnetic Poles Are On The Flip!
articles.summary: The article discusses the Sun's ongoing magnetic pole flip, a phenomenon that occurs every 11 years during solar maximum, with the northern hemisphere already having flipped. This period of heightened solar activity, marked by increased sunspots, coronal holes, and prominences, provides excellent opportunities for solar observing. The elevated activity also increases the likelihood of observing auroras, and the SIAA organizes regular solar viewing events for enthusiasts.

articles.title: SJAA Library Update
articles.summary: The SJAA Library, a growing resource, is accessible during general meetings and first Sunday solar observing/telescope fix-it sessions. The club is seeking donations of atlases, introductory books, and observing guides to support new members, and acknowledges recent contributions from William Dale Jr. and Ed Wong. Additionally, the SJAA is looking for a volunteer club librarian to manage the library.

articles.title: The Sawdust Shop
articles.summary: The article highlights The Sawdust Shop in Santa Clara, a woodworking facility founded by amateur astronomer Craig Colvin. Colvin's passion for astronomy led him to develop woodworking skills, initially to modify his own telescopes, including transforming a massive 18-inch Dobsonian into a portable design. The shop now serves as a community resource, offering tools, space, and expertise for various woodworking projects, including telescope construction, and is recommended for enthusiasts.

articles.title: Shallow Sky - Mars and Comet ISON
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for September and October, focusing on the close proximity of Mars and Comet ISON in the early morning sky, with the comet expected to brighten from 11th to 7th magnitude. It details other celestial events including Mars transiting the Beehive cluster, a Moon-Venus-Saturn conjunction, and optimal viewing for Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune. The guide also offers tips for locating challenging objects like Pluto and notes Mercury's inaccessibility.

articles.title: Meteor Shower Campout, 8/10/13
articles.summary: A meteor shower campout held on August 10, 2013, at Santa Teresa County Park was a "huge success," according to Ranger Mike Hampton. The event featured an excellent presentation by Tracy and knowledge sharing by Gene, Giny, and Ram, with the park expressing interest in hosting future star parties. The event was organized by Dave Ittner and supported by several SJAA volunteers.

articles.title: Park Service Astro-VIPs!
articles.summary: SJAA members Bill and Susan O'Neil are serving as "Astro-VIPs" at West Glacier National Park, leading extensive daily solar and night sky programs for up to 250 visitors using new Park-provided equipment. The article also details a well-attended August SJAA meeting where Dr. Christopher McKay delivered an engaging talk on the search for organic materials on Mars via the Curiosity Rover and potential future missions to Enceladus.

articles.title: Observing Targets for September Houge Park Star Parties
articles.summary: This article provides observing targets for two September star parties at Houge Park, organized by Mark Wagner. The first section details four lunar features (Copernicus, Plato, Fra Mauro, Timocharis) for a September 13 event, while the second lists four deep-sky objects (M31, Zeta Aquarrii, Double Cluster, Coathanger) for a September 27 star party, noting their visibility even in suburban skies.

articles.title: A New Star In The Sky
articles.summary: A new bright nova, discovered by Koichi Itagaki in the constellation Delphinus, has become naked-eye visible, attracting attention from amateur astronomers globally. Additionally, the article announces that the SJAA now offers a new discount for Astronomy Technology Today magazine subscriptions to its members, alongside existing discounts. Upcoming club events include the Slide and Equipment Night on October 19th and the annual Fall Swap on November 17th.

articles.title: House Star Party
articles.summary: The article recounts a heavily attended August 16th House Star Party, where participants observed celestial objects like the Moon, Saturn, and a newly discovered Nova in Delphinus, despite the bright moonlight. It also announces the beta launch of the SJAA's new website, built with a Content Management System, and solicits member feedback.

articles.title: Imaging SIG continues!
articles.summary: The SJAA announced the continuation of its Imaging Special Interest Group and received another $100 donation. The club also hosted a successful Binocular Stargazing program for 25 attendees, many new to astronomy, and a very well-attended Fix-It session where volunteers assisted 8-10 members with telescope setup, assembly, and collimation.
